items.title: Topological finite typeness over an admissible ring is tested by a single ideal of definition
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)

items.difficulty_reason: In the situation of the preceding lemma on quotients of restricted power series algebras, the lemma adds that when the source ring is admissible -- for instance adic -- the four equivalent conditions there are also equivalent to a fifth one, in which finiteness of type of the induced map of quotients is required for a single ideal of definition rather than for all of them or for a cofinal system (statement lines 6660-6669). The proof shows that the fifth condition implies the first: for an arbitrary weak ideal of definition one has to show that the corresponding map of quotients is of finite type, and since the statement for the intersection of that ideal with the chosen one implies the statement for the ideal, one may assume the arbitrary ideal is contained in the chosen one (proof lines 6671-6679). Because the chosen ideal is an ideal of definition, a power of it lies in the arbitrary one, which makes the quotient of the two ideals nilpotent, and the two kernels appearing in the evident diagram of quotients are then related as required: the small kernel is the extension of the nilpotent quotient of ideals, and the map of quotients is obtained from a finite type map by passing to a quotient by a nilpotent ideal (proof lines 6679-6692). The claim is H2: the reduction to a comparable ideal, the construction of the commutative diagram with exact rows, and the application of the nilpotent case of the finite type criterion are each displayed.
